# Improper IP address validation in validateCertificateName

`Data.X509.Validation.getNames` extracts only `AltNameDNS` entries from the
subjectAltName extension (Data/X509/Validation.hs, `unAltName`,
~L512–515 in crypton-x509-validation 1.10.1). When a certificate carries an
`iPAddress` SAN but no `dNSName` SAN, the extracted name list is empty, so
`validateNames` (~L569–580) falls through to the commonName branch as if no
SAN extension existed, even though the extension's haddock promises that the
commonName is ignored whenever subjectAltName is present. Consequently, when
a client connects to an IP literal:

* a certificate with `CN = <target IP>` but `iPAddress` SAN pointing to a
  different host is **accepted**;
* a certificate whose only valid identity is a matching `iPAddress` SAN is
  **rejected**.

Exploitation requires a certificate from a CA the client trusts that has a
commonName different from its iPAddress SAN (public CAs are barred from this
by the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, but private or enterprise
CAs can issue such certificates). A successful impersonation exposes and can
modify the protected connection.

The draft fix makes `getNames` distinguish "no SAN extension" from "SAN
extension present with no DNS names" and applies SAN semantics (including
the existing iPAddress comparison) whenever the extension is present,
restoring the documented SAN-supersedes-CN behavior in line with RFC 9525.
No fixed release is published at the time of writing (1.10.1 is the latest
release and still vulnerable).

## Credits

Reported by Dickson Wu (SEAL & CertiK). Validated and fixed by Kazu Yamamoto.
